cards.q: What do people remember about a photo they can't find?
cards.headline: A rough sense of when, plus who or what was in it.
cards.body: Rough time, a person and an object are the most remembered details (chart 1). Only 21% of stories mention two or more, but that is what people write down, not all they recall.
cards.counter: These are the details people chose to write down; the survey asks what they actually recall.
recs: Treat time as a range ("around 2019", "before the move"), not an exact date.
Use people and objects the library already knows as one-tap cues.

cards.q: What do they type into search?
cards.headline: One or two words, even when they remember more.
cards.body: 79% of the 235 quoted searches are 1–2 words (chart 2). Of 76 people who remembered two or more things, 56 still typed two words or fewer.
cards.counter: Only 235 of 1091 stories quote the exact search, so this rests on a small share of posts.
recs: Let one search hold several cues (person + place + time) as chips.
After the first word, suggest the next cue ("Riya" → "in Goa?", "around Diwali?").
Show why each result matched, so a wrong cue is easy to fix.

cards.q: Do real posts back the two branches slide 2 picked?
cards.headline: Yes: combining cues and buried results rank 1 and 2, but "not searchable" is a close third.
cards.body: Combining cues (30.4) and buried results (30.2) top the ranking, and "never backed up" is last (3.8), matching slide 2's fix / out calls (chart 3).
cards.counter: "Not searchable" has the most posts (538) and scores 29.9; slide 2 parks it on feasibility, not size.
recs: Keep combining cues and buried as the two focus branches.
Say on the slide why "not searchable" is parked: it is an indexing fix, not a search-experience one.

cards.q: Combining cues: what exactly goes wrong?
cards.headline: Search drops the second cue, and there is no way to narrow by date or place.
cards.body: Of 452 "can't combine" posts, 197 describe trying two things at once (two people, a person and a place) and 69 ask for a filter or date range. 78% of these stories end without the photo.
cards.counter: The split comes from keyword matching on the post text, so treat it as direction, not exact counts.
recs: Measure slide 2's inputs: share of multi-cue searches and zero results on them.
Prototype cue chips plus a date-range slider in the same search.

cards.q: Buried results: is it look-alikes or sheer volume?
cards.headline: Where people say why, it is volume and wrong dates more than look-alikes.
cards.body: Of 347 "buried" posts, 50 talk about too many results or long scrolls and 26 about photos in the wrong date or order; only 18 mention duplicates or look-alike shots.
cards.counter: Keyword matching, and most buried posts don't say why, so look-alikes may be under-described.
recs: Consider renaming slide 2's branch to "buried in volume" and keep look-alikes as one input.
Track scroll depth and the rank of the photo finally opened (slide 2's inputs).

cards.q: What do people do when search fails?
cards.headline: They scroll the timeline or give up.
cards.body: 73% of stories with a known ending never found the photo. Where the next step is stated, scrolling and giving up lead, and some move to another app (chart 4).
cards.counter: 287 stories did find the photo (128 easily, 159 with effort), so search works for some.
recs: Make "roughly when" a one-tap jump instead of a long scroll.
When a search misses, offer "what else do you remember?" rather than an empty page.

cards.q: Which photos are hardest to find?
cards.headline: Information photos: screenshots, IDs, bills, medicines.
cards.body: 70% of these stories end without the photo, and they usually fail because the words in them aren't searchable (chart 6).
recs: Make text in screenshots and documents searchable and say when it is.
Let people search by the app a screenshot came from.

cards.headline: People with large libraries and web / desktop users: the more photos, the more cues they need to combine.
cards.body: People with large libraries show up 1.4× more often than usual in "can't combine cues" posts (181 posts). Web / desktop users show up 1.4× more often than usual in "can't combine cues" posts (63 posts).
cards.counter: Groups are self-declared and overlap, and Android dominates because most posts come from Google Play.
recs: Pilot multi-cue search with large-library users first.
Recruit large-library users for the interviews.

cards.q: Are photos of people a memory problem or an indexing problem?
cards.headline: Mostly indexing: the photo exists but search can't see the face or name.
cards.body: 260 of 608 people and pet posts are indexing gaps: faces not grouped, names lost after a reset, old photos never processed. 89% of indexing-gap stories end without the photo.
cards.counter: The spot check found some face-grouping posts tagged off-goal, so this is undercounted, not overcounted.
recs: When a name search finds little, show likely unnamed faces to confirm in one tap.
Warn people when names were lost after a restore or reset.

cards.q: Did the new AI search (Ask Photos) help?
cards.headline: For some heavy users it made things worse.
cards.body: 520 posts say search changed or got worse, 131 of them naming Ask Photos, Gemini or AI. Their share of posts was 0–10% a year before 2023 and 14–16% since 2024 (chart 5).
cards.counter: Loud but ranks 5th: the fix is a rollback debate, not a new way to find photos.
recs: Keep exact name and date search one tap away for heavy users.
Warn users when an update changes results they relied on.

stages: Right photo buried in results / timeline
Photo isn't searchable (faces, text, place not indexed)
Can't put the memory into words

hmw.cannot_refine: How might we let one search carry everything a person remembers?
hmw.buried: How might we get people to the right stretch of time without scrolling?
hmw.index_gap: How might we make faces and words in photos findable?
hmw.misunderstood: How might we show what search understood, so a misread is fixed in one tap?
hmw.cannot_express: How might we start a search from context (what was happening, which app)?
hmw.feature_regression: How might we keep the exact searches heavy users rely on?
hmw.not_in_library: How might we tell people early that a photo was never backed up?
